text:
olivia: Hi payroll — I moved back to the US 2025-07-05 and my UK final pay (06/30) still shows PAYE + National Insurance taken. My first US payroll (07/15) also withheld Social Security. Seems like I paid both NI and US SS for the same earnings period. Can we look into whether the UK side can refund NI or if the Totalization Agreement applies?

jen-payroll: Thanks for flagging, Olivia. Can you attach your final UK payslip, P45 (if you received one), and the US 07/15 paystub? Also confirm your UK leaver date and US hire date (you said 07/05).

olivia: Uploaded final payslip and P45 to Workday (leaver date 2025-06-30). US hire date in system is 2025-07-05. Attached the 07/15 paystub showing Social Security withheld.

emma-peopleops: Adding context: for UK->US moves we normally request a certificate of coverage to avoid dual social charges, but that needs to be in place before payruns. If not, we pursue a refund through HMRC for NI or get a retro certificate.

jen-payroll: Opening ticket PR-4789 to coordinate with our UK payroll vendor and tax counsel. Initial plan: 1) confirm NI was employee liability vs employer posting, 2) ask UK vendor to submit a refund request to HMRC if NI was over-collected, 3) if HMRC refund not possible, compile an employer statement so you can claim a credit under the US foreign tax credit rules or coordinate with SSA under totalization.

uk-vendor: Received PR-4789. We'll review the payroll record for Olivia (emp id 44221) and check whether leaver was processed on the 06/30 run. If NI was applied after the leaver date due to processing lag, we'll request HMRC reclaim. HMRC reclaim timelines vary (6-12 weeks).

jen-payroll: For US side: confirm whether SSA/SS withheld is on wages for periods after 07/05 only. If there is overlap for the same earnings, tax counsel will advise whether to pursue employer refund or certificate of coverage retroactively.

olivia: Question: if HMRC refund takes months, can Redwood reimburse me in the interim and recover from HMRC later? I'd prefer not to front the cost.

jen-payroll: Operationally we can do an interim payroll credit for the NI amount if vendor confirms it's refundable and provides a timeline. We need documentation from the UK vendor showing the reclaim request. We'll document it in PR-4789 and run a reversing adjustment: "NI_reclaim_interim_credit" to your next net pay. If HMRC declines, we'd adjust accordingly.

payroll-bot: PR-4789 created by jen-payroll. Status: vendor outreach sent. Priority: high. ETA vendor response: 7 business days.

uk-vendor: Update: vendor found NI charged on 06/30 after leaver flag set but before we processed final reconciliation. We'll submit reclaim to HMRC for employer/employee NI overpayment by 2025-08-01.

jen-payroll: Thanks. Next steps for Olivia: 1) we'll post a payroll credit pending reclaim confirmation, 2) we'll provide a statement of gross earnings and NI withheld for your US tax/SS records, 3) if HMRC issues refund to employer, we'll reverse the interim credit and remit per process; if HMRC refunds directly to you, we'll reconcile.

tax-counsel: High-level note: The UK-US Totalization Agreement covers social security but you must have proof of coverage or overpayment. For tax filing, if NI cannot be recovered employer-side, you may claim a foreign tax credit on your US return for social charges depending on IRS guidance. Keep all payslips and vendor correspondence.

olivia: Thanks all. Please confirm when the payroll credit posts so I can plan. Also attaching travel docs and lease for completeness.

emma-peopleops: Got travel docs. We'll track PR-4789 and post status updates here. Expected timeline: vendor reclaim submitted 2025-08-01, HMRC response 6-12 weeks. Interim credit posting: next payroll 2025-08-15 pending vendor confirmation.

payroll-bot: PR-4789 update: vendor submitted reclaim to HMRC on 2025-08-01. Interim credit scheduled for 2025-08-15. Owner: jen-payroll.

olivia: Really appreciate it 

jen-payroll: We'll notify you as soon as HMRC responds and when any W-2/P60 or corrective forms are needed.
